chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhal, from 'Ali ibn Ya'qub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about marriage without a formal proposal (khitbah), so he said: 'Is it not that most of our young men marry while we are picking at food on the tray, saying,
ai.seo_question: Is a formal marriage proposal (khitbah) required for a valid Shia marriage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the flexibility of marriage customs by citing the prevalent practice of his time, where a simple verbal request during a meal sufficed as a proposal. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the essential elements of the marriage contract (aqd) and the cultural etiquette (adab) of the proposal (khitbah), emphasizing that validity rests on mutual consent rather than rigid ceremonial forms.
